lanes.alt: Three systems drawn as rows. In each, a proposal runs dashed up to one vertical line, is held at a gate, and continues solid only after it. Capital: an import plan is held until my click, valid 30 minutes. Sentinel: flagged prices are held by an evaluator that defaults to suppress. Cosmos: a delivery from an agent at a station is held until its contract passes, and a stop waits for me.

capital.proposes: an import plan, read from a statement

cosmos.proposes: a delivery from an agent at a station
cosmos.held: its contract passes · a stop waits for me

capital.alt: Capital. Left of the line, an import plan proposed by the assistant: five rows separated by dashed rules, 37 more below, a note that it is waiting for my click, and a Confirm import button. On the line, one gate: my click, valid 30 minutes. Right of the line, 42 ledger rows, and above them the same ledger drawn as a cash-flow diagram from income, through two companies and the person, to spending, investments and surplus. All rows and amounts are invented.
capital.assistant: the assistant: 26 tools · capped at US$0.50 and 12 tool iterations a turn

sentinel.alt: Sentinel. Left of the line, the data pipeline: seven kinds of public record, five of the processing steps and the six analysis engines, with one job running from tenders to price ranges. The price engine sends dashed candidates to the line. On the line, an evaluator whose default is to suppress: the candidates it does not confirm stop there. One continues, solid, to an alert written as a point to review. Invented example, no real tender, company or person.

alert.body1: Awarded at 1.8 times the median of 23 comparable purchases.
alert.body2: Worth checking the item specification first.

cosmos.alt: Cosmos. Top: the example line. Three stations left of the line, each a typed contract with a worker: plan with Pietra the planner, implement with Caio the implementer, review with Vera the reviewer, joined by dashed deliveries, with a return loop from review to implement at most twice. On the line, one gate: every contract passed and the pull request action is pre-authorized. Right of the line: a draft pull request, opened by the line and merged by a person. Bottom: a real run from 11 October 2026, translated from the command line. The implementer is refused a command outside its authority and escalates with a question. The line stops and waits for me, then resumes with my answer and opens the draft pull request.

playbook.alt: The validation playbook on a time axis from day 0 to week 4, where the line is the go, pivot or kill decision. MilhasGrupo runs dashed from one page, through a prototype and paid traffic, and ends on the line in a hollow ring: its verdict is not recorded yet. FIRE-BR is a short dashed stroke: one page, June 2026.

agents.alt: Working with coding agents. Left of the line, six dashed branches fan out from a written contract, CLAUDE.md, read first since August 2026. On the line, one gate: lint, typecheck and tests, then my merge. Five branches pass and merge, solid, into main, 80 merged. One stops at the gate: closed, not merged.
agents.gate: lint · typecheck · tests, then my merge

deploy.alt: Deploys. Left of the line: git pull and build, then a migrate step drawn dashed because the new version is still a proposal. On the line, one gate: the migration exits zero. Right of the line, one machine at home with 21 services behind a tunnel with no inbound ports, four databases each with a dev twin, and 53 uptime monitors generated from one spec. A second dashed path stops at the line: if the migration fails, the old version keeps running.
